forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: the SE groundswell that made Sunday is already leaking away, and the wind has turned from friend to nuisance. Primary is 3.8ft at 10 seconds from 146° SSE — still a usable angle, well east of dead south — but energy is on a one-way slide: 195 kJ at 6am, 157 by 9am, 110 at noon, 82 by 3pm. Consistency is a flat 100%, so what's there is reliable, it's just shrinking hour by hour. Wind is light NW offshore at first light (6 gusting 8 kph), then it backs NNW and goes cross-shore through the morning — 8 gusting 16 at 9am, 10 gusting 21 by noon — before swinging back WNW offshore 13 gusting 22 in the afternoon, by which point the swell has bled out. Dawn to 8am is the session; everything after that is a downgrade. Long Reef is the pick at 4–6ft and the only spot Surfline rates fair-to-good through the morning, with Curl Curl fair-to-good at 6am only. Dee Why is an honest 3–4ft, Manly the smallest at 2–4ft. Tide runs low 0.24m at 5:04am and fills to a 1.39m high at 11:17am, so the dawn window is on the push — good for the open banks. Water 17.6°C (SharkSmart median across 29 stations, 15.5–19.8 spread), air 11°C at 6am rising to 21°C by noon under clear sky. Tomorrow is a write-off — 1–3ft and 23 kJ. 🦈 SharkSmart NSW read clean: zero detections Palm Beach → Manly in the last 24h across all five feeds. ✈️ Reminder: you're in Oahu until 13 Aug — use /hawaii-surf over there. ⚠️ This note is composed from live Surfline point data (wave / wind / tide / weather JSON), not quoted from a Surfline forecaster. The free forecast window ends Sat 8 Aug, so Saturday is scraped but Sunday is a trend projection.

wind.summary: Light NW offshore at first light — 6 gusting 8 kph at 6am, the only genuinely glassy hour. Backs NNW and turns cross-shore by 9am (8 gusting 16), 10 gusting 21 by noon, then swings back WNW offshore 13 gusting 22 mid-afternoon once the swell has already gone. Dawn to 8am or don't bother.

shark.summary: No shark detections logged anywhere between Palm Beach and Manly in the last 24 hours. SMART drumline (SSPRO2), DPI/SLS drone (DPINSW), Surf Life Saving NSW (SLSNSW2), trauma and events feeds all fetched cleanly this refresh with zero Northern Beaches hits.

days.label: Today
days.note: Yesterday's leftovers, and they're draining fast. 3.8ft at 10 seconds from 146° with 157 kJ at 9am — down from 195 at dawn and only 82 by mid-afternoon — at a perfect 100% consistency. The wind is the problem: light NW offshore at 6am, cross-shore NNW from 9am, 10 gusting 21 by noon. First light through 8am is the whole session. Tide is on the push from a 5:04am low to an 11:17am high, which favours the open banks over the Point. Long Reef is the only spot holding a proper wave; Manly is the fallback if you want size you can ignore.

swells.label: The engine — 146° is a workable angle for the Point, but 10 seconds isn't enough push to bend hard
Short-period E windswell — fills the gaps, adds slop
NE windchop riding the cross-shore breeze
20-second S background pulse — too small and too far south to matter today

dee-why.window: 6–8am, and be honest that it's a fair day not a good one. Energy is already falling when you paddle out (195 kJ at 6am, 157 by 9am), and the NNW goes cross-shore from 9am. The Point won't get much out of a 10-second 146°, so the beach banks between the Point and the pool are the better read on the tide push.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Frontside at the Point, but don't wait there for something that isn't coming — 10 seconds at 146° doesn't wrap the way Sunday's 12-second did. Better call is to surf the banks and treat it as a rail-work session: 3–4ft with only 157 kJ behind it means the wave won't carry you, so generate your own speed off the bottom and keep the turns tight rather than hunting a big open face.

swells.label: The engine — the Reef takes a 146° SSE more squarely than anywhere else on the beach
NE windchop from the cross-shore breeze

long-reef.window: The clear pick and the only spot Surfline holds at fair-to-good from 6am through midday. 4–6ft while everything else is 2–4ft, and the corner keeps its shape longer once the NNW gets cross-shore. Go early — 6–9am — because energy drops from 195 to 110 kJ by noon.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Your frontside at the Reef corner, and at 4–6ft with only 157 kJ it's a size-without-consequence day — the opposite of yesterday. That means you can sit deeper and take off later than you'd dare on a heavy 12-second swell. Use it: this is the session for the turn you've been putting off, not for pick-and-choose. Watch the NNW at 9am — once it's 8 gusting 16 the corner starts to bump.

swells.label: The engine — straight into the open banks with nothing in the way

curl-curl.window: Surfline rates it fair-to-good at 6am and 4–5ft, then downgrades to fair and 3–4ft from 9am — so the dawn hour is genuinely the best of it. The upside here is the wind: the NNW stays offshore at Curl Curl all morning where it goes cross at Dee Why and Manly. North Curl Curl corner on the tide push toward the 11:17am high.
alerts: The fair-to-good read is the 6am slot only — by 9am it's fair and 3–4ft. Dawn or nothing.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Curl Curl's lefts are your backhand, and the NNW staying offshore here is the reason to choose it over Dee Why this morning. With only 157 kJ the wave won't hold you through a long bottom turn — set the rail early off the drop and go straight to the top rather than drawing it out. If the corner is soft on the early low tide, wait for the push toward 11:17am, but you'll be trading wind quality for tide.

swells.label: The engine — North Steyne sits deepest in the shadow of a 146° swell

manly.window: Smallest of the four and Surfline drops it to poor-to-fair by midday once the NNW is cross-shore. 3–4ft at 6am fading to 2–3ft. Only worth the drive if you're already in town — otherwise the Reef is 2ft bigger for the same trip.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: Backhand on the North Steyne lefts. At 2–4ft with 157 kJ this is a volume-and-flow session, not a power one — ride the extra float and prioritise linking turns over trying to force a critical section that isn't there. Go before 9am; once the NNW turns cross-shore North Steyne bumps up faster than the northern beaches.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The floor drops out. Energy collapses to 23 kJ — a seventh of today's dawn reading — with 1–3ft and consistency sliding from 80% at 9am to 57% by mid-afternoon. Primary swell is a scattered 1.4–1.6ft mix of 10-second SSE remnant and 7-second ESE windswell with nothing behind it. The one saving grace is the wind: W to WNW offshore 6–9 kph all morning and no sea breeze until late. Glassy and clean, but there's almost nothing to be clean on. Groveller day at best.

dee-why.window: Knee-to-thigh and 23 kJ. Clean under the W/WNW offshore all morning but there is genuinely not much wave. Slides to poor-to-fair by 3pm. Skip unless you just want water time.

long-reef.window: Still the size leader by a foot, which on a 23 kJ day is the difference between a surf and a swim. Morning W offshore is light and clean. The only spot on the coast worth the paddle tomorrow.

curl-curl.window: Matches Long Reef for size but on open banks with no corner to organise it. Clean W/WNW offshore all morning. North Curl Curl if the bank is holding, otherwise it's a paddle.

manly.window: Knee-high and soft. Nothing here tomorrow.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is now inside the 6-day window and scraped live; Sunday still sits beyond it and is a projection. Sat 8 Aug reads small but immaculate: 2.6–2.8ft at 8 seconds from 172–174° with 40–50 kJ, plus a 1–2ft E/ENE windswell at 70–89°, under W/WNW offshore of just 3–7 kph all morning. Glassy, gutless, and dead-south — 173° is the angle that gets eaten by the Dee Why headland, so expect the Point to under-perform and the open banks to carry the day. Long Reef edges it at 3–4ft early. Midweek is the build to watch: Thu 6 Aug brings 3.6–3.8ft at 9s from 183° and Fri 7 Aug 4.4ft at 9s from 179° with 176 kJ and W offshore mornings — both dead-south again. Re-check Thursday for whether the weekend rebuilds or keeps easing.

dee-why.window: Saturday scrapes as 2–3ft with 40 kJ and W/WNW offshore at 6 kph — glassy but small, and a 173° dead-south angle is the one the headland eats here. Open banks over the Point. Sunday is unscraped; if the midweek south pulse holds it stays similar, but treat it as direction not detail.
